title: A bacterium that degrades and assimilates poly(ethylene terephthalate)
authors: Yoshida, S., Hiraga, K., Takehana, T., Taniguchi, I., Yamaji, H., Maeda, Y., Toyohara, K., Miyamoto, K., Kimura, Y., & Oda, K.
abstract_summary: Isolation of Ideonella sakaiensis 201-F6 from environmental consortium capable of growing on low-crystallinity PET films. Identification of two core hydrolytic enzymes: PETase (ISF6_4831) and MHETase (ISF6_0224).
key_findings: I. sakaiensis 201-F6 utilizes PET as primary carbon and energy source for growth.
ISF6_4831 (PETase) converts PET into mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (MHET) with minor yields of bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) and terephthalic acid (TPA).
ISF6_0224 (MHETase) further hydrolyzes MHET into monomeric TPA and ethylene glycol (EG).
Native PETase shows higher catalytic activity towards low-crystallinity (amorphous) PET film at 30°C than cutinases from Thermobifida fusca or lipases.

title: Characterization and engineering of a plastic-degrading aromatic polyesterase
authors: Austin, H. P., Allen, M. D., Donohoe, B. S., Rorrer, N. A., LeFebvre, F. L., Schwab, B. C., Jayasinghe, R., Eaton, B. L., Gallagher, D. J., Halliwell, R. T., Johnson, C. W., Smith, P. G., Michener, C. A., Sun, Y., & McGeehan, J. B.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)
abstract_summary: High-resolution crystal structure determination (0.92 Å) of Ideonella sakaiensis PETase revealing a more open active-site cleft compared to canonical cutinases, and structure-guided protein engineering producing double mutant S238F/W159H with increased catalytic activity.
key_findings: PETase active site cleft is notably wider (~3-5 Å wider) than homologous cutinases, accommodating aromatic polyester chains.
Conservation of the canonical Ser160-His237-Asp206 catalytic triad within an alpha/beta-hydrolase fold.
Engineered variant S238F/W159H exhibited enhanced degradation of post-consumer PET bottle material.
Demonstrated enzymatic degradation capability on bio-based polyester polyethylene 2,5-furandicarboxylate (PEF).
Wild-type PETase thermotolerance is constrained; thermal denaturation onset observed between 42°C and 48°C.

title: An engineered PET depolymerase to break down and recycle plastic bottles
authors: Tournier, V., Topham, C. M., Gilles, A., David, B., Folgoas, C., Moya-Leclair, E., Kamionka, E., Desrousseaux, M., Texier, H., Gavalda, S., Cot, M. N., Guémard, E., Dalibey, M., Nomme, J., Vivani, G., et al.
abstract_summary: Development of an engineered leaf-branch compost cutinase (LCC-ICCG: F243I/D238C/S283C/Y127G) operating at elevated temperatures (72°C) near the glass transition temperature of PET, achieving 90% depolymerization within 10 hours.
key_findings: Engineered disulfide bridge (D238C/S283C) elevated melting temperature (Tm) by 9.8°C to allow prolonged reaction at 72°C.
Depolymerization at 72°C exploits polymer chain mobility near the PET glass transition temperature (Tg ~67-75°C).
Demonstrated recycling loop: recycled terephthalic acid purified from digest was re-polymerized into virgin-quality transparent PET bottles.
Activity highly dependent on neutral-to-slightly basic pH (optimum around pH 8.0) and rapid base titration to neutralize released terephthalic acid.

experimental_conditions_reported.buffer: 100 mM potassium phosphate buffer with automated NaOH neutralization

title: Machine learning-aided engineering of hydrolases for PET depolymerization
authors: Lu, H., Diaz, D. J., Czarnecki, N. J., Zhu, C., Kim, W., Shroff, R., Acosta, D. J., Alexander, B. R., Cole, H. O., Zhang, Y., et al.
abstract_summary: Structure-based machine learning algorithm (MutCompute) utilized to engineer FAST-PETase (N233K/R224Q/S121E/D186H/R280A), conferring superior thermal stability and catalytic depolymerization rate at 50°C across untreated post-consumer plastics.
key_findings: FAST-PETase contains 5 consensus and scaffold-stabilizing mutations yielding a melting temperature increase of 8.8°C over wild type.
Achieved depolymerization across 51 diverse untreated post-consumer PET items.
Operates efficiently in an intermediate temperature regime (40-50°C), reducing thermal energy input compared to thermophilic cutinases.
Robust activity retained across pH range of 6.5 to 8.0.

title: Structure of the plastic-degrading enzyme MHETase and its catalytic mechanism
authors: Palm, G. J., Reisky, L., Böttcher, D., Müller, H., Michels, E. A. P., Walczak, M. C., Berndt, M. D., Weiss, F., Bornscheuer, U. T., & Weber, G.
abstract_summary: Structural and functional characterization of Ideonella sakaiensis MHETase (PDB: 6QGA) resolving the molecular mechanism for hydrolysis of mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate to terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol.
key_findings: MHETase belongs to the alpha/beta-hydrolase superfamily with an engineered lid domain providing substrate specificity.
Strict substrate specificity for mono-(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (MHET); minimal activity on intact PET polymers.
Active site residues Ser225, His528, and Asp492 form the canonical catalytic triad.
Relieves product inhibition on PETase: accumulation of MHET slows PETase rate; co-incubation with MHETase accelerates net PET breakdown.

title: Analysis of the biodegradation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) by Ideonella sakaiensis
authors: Taniguchi, I., Yoshida, S., Hiraga, K., Miyamoto, K., Kimura, Y., & Oda, K.
abstract_summary: Comprehensive analysis of PET biodegradation kinetics by Ideonella sakaiensis cells and purified enzymes, evaluating surface morphology, crystallinity boundaries, and enzyme secretion dynamics.
key_findings: PETase preferentially attacks ester linkages in the mobile, amorphous surface regions of PET.
High-crystallinity biaxially oriented PET (BOPET) exhibits markedly slower hydrolysis than amorphous PET.
Secreted PETase adheres to the polymer surface via hydrophobic residues flanking the catalytic groove.
Metabolic flux in vivo channels TPA via 1,2-dioxygenase pathway to protocatechuic acid and Krebs cycle intermediates.

experimental_conditions_reported.buffer: Mineral salt medium with low-crystallinity PET film
experimental_conditions_reported.substrate_type: Commercial amorphous and crystalline PET specimens

title: The Current State of Research on PET Hydrolyzing Enzymes Available for Biorecycling
authors: Kawai, F., Kawabata, T., & Oda, M.
abstract_summary: Review and comparative benchmark of polyester hydrolases, cutinases, and esterases capable of PET depolymerization, contrasting mesophilic PETases with thermophilic bacterial cutinases.
key_findings: Depolymerization rate strongly correlates with reaction temperature relative to PET glass transition temperature (Tg ~65-75°C in water).
Mesophilic enzymes (e.g. wild-type IsPETase) operate below Tg where polymer chain flexibility is low, requiring longer incubation.
Thermophilic enzymes (e.g., LCC, TfCut2) operate near Tg where chain accessibility is substantially elevated.
Acidification from produced terephthalic acid requires active buffering to prevent enzyme inactivation.
